A.summary: Unions are monopolistic suppliers of labor that extract higher wages for members, while non-members and non-union workers earn lower wages in the competitive market.

B.summary: Unions are collective representatives that increase overall productivity, raising wage levels for all workers at unionized firms so members and non-members earn similar wages.

c1.text: Labor unions are monopolistic suppliers of labor that exercise monopoly power in supplying labor within their membership.

c2.text: The labor of non-members and non-union workers is traded in a competitive market.

c3.text: Unions can extract higher wages for members than the competitive market wage.

c4.text: Labor displaced by higher union wages enters the competitive market, lowering competitive market wages and increasing the wage premium.

c5.text: Union members earn higher wages than non-members and non-union workers, while non-members and non-union workers have similar wages.

c6.text: Labor unions are a system of collective representation that demands equal pay for equal work and represents minorities.

c7.text: Union activities raise worker satisfaction, prevent arbitrary changes, and increase overall worker productivity.

c8.text: Increased worker productivity naturally raises overall wage levels across the unionized company.

c9.text: At unionized companies, wages of union members and non-members are relatively similar, and both are higher than wages of non-union workers.

a.note: Survey results confirm A's predicted wage structure (members > non-members ≈ non-union) and contradict B's prediction (members ≈ non-members > non-union).

b.note: A makes no claims or predictions about gender wage differentials, so finding a smaller gap among members neither strengthens nor weakens A.

c.note: B explicitly predicts that union activities raise company-wide productivity so that members and non-members earn similar wages; hence this finding does not weaken B.

h1.text: A survey comparing workers of similar occupations and skill levels found that union members' wages are higher than those of non-members, and there is no wage difference between non-members and non-union workers.

h2.text: A survey on the gender wage gap among workers of similar occupation and skill level found that the gender wage gap is smaller among union members than among non-members.

h3.text: A survey of workers at companies with unions found that the wages of union members are similar to those of non-members with similar occupations and skill.
